newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Primakov says Russia still against NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Primakov says Russia still against NATO expansion.

text.p: Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, who held talks in Moscow this week with NATO Secretary-General Javier Solana, said on Wednesday that Russia remained firmly opposed to the alliance's planned eastward expansion.
"Russia stood and stands against the enlargement of NATO...on geopolitical, military and moral-psychological grounds," Primakov said in remarks broadcast on television.
"We fear that (expansion) will create new dividing lines in Europe. And we have grounds for concern," he added.
Primakov, reiterating Moscow's line in his first statement since meeting Solana, said any future document that aimed to define NATO-Russian relations should be legally binding.
"Our opponents (in NATO) fear that this will be very difficult to realise because it must be ratified by the 16 parliaments of the alliance's member states," Primakov said.
But he added that the same parliaments would be required to ratify the accession of the new members.
NATO is expected to issue formal invitations to the Czech Republic, Hungary and Poland at its next summit scheduled for July in Madrid.
NATO officials have made clear that Moscow's objections will not change the schedule. They say steps towards enlargement will start even if talks with Russia do not bear fruit before the summit.
Primakov held five hours of talks with Solana at an official residence outside Moscow on Monday. The two men decided a timetable for further Moscow-NATO discussions on the issue.
Officials in Brussels said Solana had presented detailed proposals on a permanent consultative mechanism to help Russia accept the alliance's expansion.
"We have embarked on a serious dialogue and we will pursue it further," Primakov said on Wednesday.
